items.title: Howard Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019
items.q: I thought it was really interesting on his “Stolen Moments” you know first you have Freddie Hubbard... [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah. I use those solo notes as background notes in my arrangement of “Stolen Moments.”

ctx.x: Well it’s a composition and that sort of thing from Nadia Boulanger. And was able to use a lot of what he learned in his own music, I mean his music would have been different without that. And at the same time he was making records with Jimmy Forrest and King Curtis, you know, down home boogie stuff. But I loved his writing.

I thought it was really interesting on his “Stolen Moments” you know first you have Freddie Hubbard, then you had Eric Dolphy and they’re like all over the place sort of, and then he comes in just with his [scats].
Yeah. I use those solo notes as background notes in my arrangement of “Stolen Moments.” Do you know that one at all?
